In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the brain abscesses caused by Bacillus species are rare, but not extremely rare, and the clinical features of the brain abscess are nonspecific.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Bacillus genus should be considered as a causative organism of brain abscess.
a penetrating injury should be considered even in cases of delayed presentation, and that a brain abscess should be considered even when the initial symptoms are not typical.
a brain abscess caused by Bacillus species should be considered in patients with a history of penetrating injury and a prolonged course of symptoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Bacillus species are rare causes of brain abscess and that Bacillus macerens should be added to the list of rare causes of brain infection.
Bacillus spp. should be considered in the differential diagnosis of brain abscess.
Bacillus spp., especially B. macerans, can cause brain abscesses, and the diagnosis can be delayed due to the lack of specific signs and symptoms.
